title: Mildred as a quick study on record dates
summary: On recording days she barely rehearsed; Norvo or pianist Bill Miller played the song once and she recorded it.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: So, let's go on talking about Mildred's performance and one thing you said a little earlier about her recording, you know, you said -- tell me what you -- we didn't put that on tape when you said that she would just look at the music --

Well she, I think from working on those early radio shows, with Paul and all. She really was a quick study as far as -- as recording is concerned. I know a lot of times, we'd be in the morning of the date and she'd be upstairs dressing and she'd say, 'Play the tunes.' She hadn't run over them, yet. That was the morning we record -- an

afternoon we were recording, so I'd go to the piano and play them over for her. She'd be upstairs, she'd listen, that's all. Then she'd come down and she'd take the tune -- the numbers and she'd read the lyrics to herself. Maybe while she was having breakfast. And that would be it. Maybe we'd go to the tune, the piano player who was Bill Miller at that time, would play them through for her. Just once and she'd just follow him. And we'd start -- Eddie would be rehearsing the arrangement, we hadn't ever played it before. Made for the date. And she'd go over it and that's the way she'd record. Gone from to the other like that.
Yeah, I should think it did. As you said, how many singers have to live with a number and rehearse it --
They would go through the number and they would memorize the lyrics, and they'd get off --
But she was cool about all of it, she never got shook up about these things. Never at all. She was fast in learning lyrics. Very fast.
Did she not suffer from nerves, then, in performing?
No, I don't think -- I think just -- not the nerves in -- as we think, just a little tick of nervousness in everybody, that anticipation -- that kind of holds the

Especially in her case. I think she'd get nervous before (unintelligible), if she would -- oh, maybe I don't know, doing new things or -- I think she was more concerned with getting if nervous that the music was wrong.
Think she was more concerned with that.
